explanation: Cheek-kissing (beijo no rosto) is the standard social greeting in Brazil, typically between women, and between men and women, starting on the right cheek. It signals warmth and is expected even among new acquaintances in social settings; declining it outright can come across as cold, though a handshake is the norm in formal business contexts.
local_tip: Lean in starting with the right cheek and make a light kissing sound without pressing your lips to the skin, and follow the local kiss count rather than assuming it's always just one.
regional_note: The number of kisses varies by region: one is typical in São Paulo, two in Rio de Janeiro, and three or more in Bahia and other parts of the Northeast.

also_check.note: Cheek kissing is not customary; a bow or handshake is the standard greeting.
Cheek kissing (la bise) is common, though the number of kisses varies by region (typically two to four).
Kissing between unrelated men and women is not done; follow local gender norms closely.
